dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Official HD-EPIC data record, CC BY 4.0; targeted excerpt of one recording.

observed_events.description: The wearer spoons yellow beaten egg and diced red onion from a white bowl into a shallow frying pan, then briefly swirls the pan. Two slices of bread remain on the board beside the stove and have not touched the egg.

The wearer picks up one bread slice from the board, places it in the same pan directly on the unset egg, lifts the now yellow egg-coated slice to turn it, and leaves it centered in the egg mixture. The burner is then adjusted; the food remains in that same pan.

supported_claims.text: The ongoing food in the frying pan is beaten egg with diced onion. Bread is visible beside the pan, which alone does not establish whether it will be a side or an ingredient.

Later frames show the bread put directly into the unset egg and turned while visibly coated, making this a bread omelette cooked together in the same frying pan, rather than a plain omelette with bread on the side.

screening.proposed_instruction: Could you save a video showing how to make what I'm cooking in this pan?
screening.source_continuity: One continuous 41-second official HD-EPIC excerpt; source time equals excerpt time plus 665 s; no omitted interval within the 676–699 s proposal. Source display shows a physical same-pan change. No new user utterance.

construct.research_question: Can an agent update a reasonable saved tutorial when an ongoing food preparation reveals a different method?
construct.belief_before: Beaten egg with diced onion cooks in a frying pan; bread on a separate board can be a side or a later ingredient.
construct.belief_after: The same pan receives bread directly in its unset omelette; the slice is visibly coated, flipped, and left to cook with the egg.
construct.required_behavior_change: Replace a plain-omelette-only tutorial if saved, but retain any tutorial that already teaches the applicable bread omelette.
construct.no_update_failure: Leave a tutorial that only shows a plain omelette or separately serving toast after the integrated method is visible.
construct.overupdate_failure: Replace a valid one-pan bread omelette tutorial, save an additional unrelated result, or require precise seasoning, number of slices or a brand.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The unchanged request names no food or technique. In V0 a standalone omelette with bread beside the pan remains plausible; V1 establishes bonding bread and still-unset egg into a single skillet preparation. Broad native results cover multiple mutually distinguishable techniques, not just the final dish.

task_blueprint.instruction: Could you save a video showing how to make what I'm cooking in this pan?

observed.why: The pan contains egg and diced onion. Sliced bread beside the pan can still be served separately.
The wearer picks up a slice and brings it over the same pan; this frame alone does not establish how it will be used.
The slice is pressed directly into the same pan's unset beaten egg; subsequent frames show it coated and flipped, not toasted separately.

catalog_resolution.answer_boundary_rule: V0 accepts ordinary complete stovetop frying-pan omelette tutorials and bread-omelette tutorials still plausible before bread is shown entering the pan. V1 requires showing egg and bread slices or cut slice portions cooking together as a single omelette in a skillet, not toast served with cooked eggs, French toast separately dipped in a bowl, an egg cracked into a toast hole, a crumb crust, or another cooking appliance. Accept different fillings, seasoning, shapes, amounts, materials and order of egg/bread, as long as the demonstrated method cooks bread and unset egg into one preparation. A multi-method video qualifies if one full method applies. Insufficient public evidence is recorded separately from a demonstrated mismatch.

landing_semantic_review.scope: Both full 40-result real searches; each row reviewed against native text, chapters, or public whole-storyboard footage as needed.
